y-m-02-03.title: One book wey dey third from left, which position e be from right?
y-m-02-03.topic: Position and order: saying position based on one reference
y-m-02-03.goal: Talk about di same spot using number wey you count from left and number wey you count from right, find di pattern between di two numbers, make several possible spots, and find cases wey information no complete.
y-m-02-03.material: 7 books dey stand in one row for one shelf inside bookcase. Left and right mean left and right as you stand in front of bookcase. Di books dey one continuous row with no space. Mina count di blue book from left and talk 'second', and Seohyeon count from right and talk 'sixth'. Both count am correctly.
y-m-02-03.thinking.0: Knowing say when reference change, di words wey you use to name di same thing change too
y-m-02-03.thinking.1: Make several spots wey fit one condition
y-m-02-03.prereq.1: Words wey show order like first, second, third
y-m-02-03.s.s1.prompt: Could the books Mina and Seohyeon talk about be same book?
y-m-02-03.s.s1.hint.0: Draw 7 books as 7 circles and write 1,2,3,... from left. 1 2
y-m-02-03.s.s1.hint.1: On same circles, write numbers counted from right too, find the second spot.
y-m-02-03.s.s1.o.a: Different books. Second and sixth different places
y-m-02-03.s.s1.r.a: You think different counting numbers mean different places. You think about which side person count from?
y-m-02-03.s.s1.o.b: Could be same book. Dem count from opposite sides
y-m-02-03.s.s1.r.b: This idea say if counting side different, same book fit get different number.
y-m-02-03.s.s1.o.c: You no fit tell because you no know how many books dey
y-m-02-03.s.s1.r.c: You miss info say 7 books dey. Check whether needed info already dey for this situation.
y-m-02-03.s.s1.explain: If row get 7 books, 5 books dey right of second from left. From right, that book get 5 books before am, so na sixth. Numbers different because side wey dem count from different; na same book.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.prompt: One red book dey same bookshelf (7 books). Make 2 different places so red book dey left of middle (fourth). Put place from left as a, place from right as b. Both numbers gats point same book.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.hint.0: First write left and right counting numbers together on row of 7 circles.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.hint.1: First count how many places dey left of middle (fourth).
y-m-02-03.s.s2.ok.c1: Number counted from left between 1 and 7.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.fail.c1: Number counted from left gats be natural number 1 to 7.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.ok.c2: Number counted from right between 1 and 7.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.fail.c2: Number counted from right gats be natural number 1 to 7.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.ok.c3: Two numbers point to same one book.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.fail.c3: These two numbers no point to same book. Write dem on row of 7 books and check.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.fail.c4: E no dey left of middle (fourth).
y-m-02-03.s.s2.explain: Possible places na three: (1,7),(2,6),(3,5). Fourth place na fourth from left and right too, so e no be "left of middle."
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.prompt: Use numbers to write how b get decided once a set, the pattern between two numbers.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write pairs of numbers for two places you make side by side, compare their relation.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.hint.1: Check wetin happen to right number when left number increase by 1.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.placeholder: For example, if e na ...th from left, e na ...th from right.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: The pattern you write correct for both or more places you make?
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You write say pattern only apply when 7 books dey?
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.model.0: If na 3rd from left, na 5th from right. When you add both numbers, always 8.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.model.1: Each time left number go up 1, right number go down 1. Like 1st and 7th, 2nd and 6th.
y-m-02-03.s.s2.because.modelNote.1: This say how e change without using sum. E valid too.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.prompt: For another bookshelf, you no know how many books. Only know green book third from left. Can you say which place from right?
y-m-02-03.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine add one more book at right end, and check if green book place from left change.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.hint.1: Draw case with 5 books and 7 books and compare right-side place.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.o.a: You fit say only if you know total book count
y-m-02-03.s.s3.r.a: You check whether info enough and state wetin missing.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.o.b: Assume other shelf also get 7 books and say e fifth from right
y-m-02-03.s.s3.r.b: You carry earlier shelf's 7 books over to this one. Nobody say how many books this shelf get.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.o.c: Maybe e third from right too
y-m-02-03.s.s3.r.c: You use left-side number same for right. Think what happen if e no be middle book.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.o.d: Whatever book count, right-side place stay fixed
y-m-02-03.s.s3.r.d: You think number stay same as book count grow. Think wetin happen if add one book to right.
y-m-02-03.s.s3.explain: If you know only e third from left, you no know how many books dey right. If 5 books total, e third from right; if 7, e fifth from right. You fit decide only when total book count known.

y-m-02-05.title: If end mark bigger, e longer?
y-m-02-05.goal: Understand info about only one endpoint no enough to compare lengths; state you need know where each starts too, update first judgment with new info, and choose direct comparison method.
y-m-02-05.material: On desk, pencil 가 and 나 lie straight side by side next to ruler. Ruler marks 0 to 10, equal spaces. For now you only see right ends: 가 end at mark 9; 나 end at mark 8. You never see left ends. Eunseo say, "가 reach 9, so e longer."
y-m-02-05.thinking.1: Update your judgment with new info
y-m-02-05.prereq.0: Meaning of 0 on ruler and one gap between marks
y-m-02-05.s.s1.prompt: Wetin else you need to know to decide whether Eunseo correct?
y-m-02-05.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine one pencil on ruler; say how many marks you need know to know its length.
y-m-02-05.s.s1.hint.1: Compare length if left end of pencil ending at 9 dey at 0 versus at 7.
y-m-02-05.s.s1.o.a: Whether both pencils get same thickness
y-m-02-05.s.s1.r.a: Thickness no use to compare length. Length depend where object start and end.
y-m-02-05.s.s1.o.b: How many spaces left to ruler end (mark 10)
y-m-02-05.s.s1.r.b: You already know right end mark, so this repeats same info. Does e add anything new?
y-m-02-05.s.s1.o.c: At which mark left end of each pencil dey
y-m-02-05.s.s1.r.c: You see both start and end positions needed.
y-m-02-05.s.s1.o.d: Which pencil sharpened to sharper point
y-m-02-05.s.s1.r.d: You need look where pencil sit, no be sharpness. Think info needed to read length from marks.
y-m-02-05.s.s1.explain: Length run from pencil start place to end place. Right-end mark alone no tell which longer; you need know left-end mark.
y-m-02-05.s.s2.prompt: Now left ends known. 가 start at mark 5, 나 at mark 0. Seohyeon think again. Choose line in Seohyeon words wey hard to trust.
y-m-02-05.s.s2.hint.0: Point with your finger at marks from which to which 가 and 나 each lie, and count spaces.
y-m-02-05.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether pencil with greater end mark also start same place.
y-m-02-05.s.s2.line.2: 가, wey end mark bigger, longer.
y-m-02-05.s.s2.explain: Lines 3 and 4 hard to trust. Lines 1 and 2 read marks accurately. 가 goes 5 to 9, so 4 spaces; 나 goes 0 to 8, so 8 spaces. Line 3 compare only ending marks and ignore starting place, so line 4 conclusion no reliable too. New info mean we gats revise Eunseo first judgment.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.prompt: Without ruler, how you fit place two pencils to compare lengths reliably? Choose every good method.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine wetin change if put two pencils side by side with one end against desk corner.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.hint.1: When one end same line, where on remaining ends you look to compare length?
y-m-02-05.s.s3.o.a: Line up left ends on same line and look at right ends
y-m-02-05.s.s3.r.a: This idea say once one end line up, compare position of other end only.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.o.b: Line up right ends on same line and look at left ends
y-m-02-05.s.s3.r.b: This idea say you fit line up either end.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.o.c: Put pencils far apart and look with eyes
y-m-02-05.s.s3.r.c: From far, dem look different depending where dem dey and your eye level. Is that same as putting side by side?
y-m-02-05.s.s3.o.d: Just say pencil with right end further out longer
y-m-02-05.s.s3.r.d: You carry over same mistake from ruler problem: looking only at right end.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.explain: If one end line up, pencil whose other end stick out further longer. Either end fit line up. Far apart or looking at one end alone no reliable.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.acc.0: Lining up left ends reliable. Good to know right ends give same comparison.
y-m-02-05.s.s3.acc.1: Lining up right ends reliable too. Good to know left ends give same comparison.

y-m-02-01.title: Long or slanted cards too na quadrilaterals?
y-m-02-01.topic: Plane shapes: recognizing di shape of quadrilateral
y-m-02-01.goal: Find di wrong line for one idea wey narrowly think quadrilateral mean 'upright with four sides of di same length', set standard to judge by number of straight lines and pointed corners, and explain long or slanted quadrilaterals.
y-m-02-01.material: Harin gather three quadrilateral cards. Card 가 dey upright and all four straight lines get di same length. Card 나 long sideways, so top and bottom lines long and two side lines short. Card 다 get di same shape as 가 but e slant so one pointed corner dey on top. All three cards get four straight lines around dem and four pointed corners. (No picture dey, so imagine am with words.) Harin think like dis.
y-m-02-01.thinking.0: Check whether each line for solution get reason
y-m-02-01.thinking.1: Choose standard for judging and test with dat standard
y-m-02-01.thinking.2: Make and explain one example of another shape wey fit di standard, using words
y-m-02-01.prereq.0: You fit recognize triangle, quadrilateral, and circle shapes and talk their names.
y-m-02-01.prereq.1: You fit count 'straight lines' and 'pointed corners' by pointing to dem with finger. (Counting numbers up to 4)
y-m-02-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose di one line for Harin thinking wey hard to trust. (Two lines fit hard to trust.)
y-m-02-01.s.s1.hint.0: For di three cards, point with your finger and count how many straight lines and pointed corners dey.
y-m-02-01.s.s1.hint.1: For each line, separate whether Harin reason na something 'counted' or 'feeling from how e look'.
y-m-02-01.s.s1.line.0: Card 가 get four straight lines and four pointed corners, so e na quadrilateral.
y-m-02-01.s.s1.line.1: Card 나 long sideways, so e no be quadrilateral.
y-m-02-01.s.s1.line.2: Card 다 slant, but e get four straight lines and four pointed corners.
y-m-02-01.s.s1.line.3: So quadrilateral must get all four straight lines di same length.
y-m-02-01.s.s1.explain: Lines 2 and 4 hard to trust. Dem talk lines 1 and 3 after counting straight lines and pointed corners. Dem decide line 2 only by looking say 'e long', and line 4 stretch wetin dem see for card 가 alone to say 'all must get same length'. Even if e long or slant, four straight lines and four pointed corners still dey.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.prompt: When you dey decide whether card 나 na quadrilateral, wetin most reliable thing to look?
y-m-02-01.s.s2.hint.0: Look for wetin no dey change even if you turn card 나 or draw am bigger.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.hint.1: Talk wetin be the same and wetin different for cards 가, 나, and 다.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.o.a: Check whether e get same size as di first quadrilateral card wey you see
y-m-02-01.s.s2.r.a: Size no be clue to decide di name of shape. Big quadrilateral and small quadrilateral both na quadrilateral.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.o.b: Check whether di direction wey dem put di card correct
y-m-02-01.s.s2.r.b: Di shape remain the same even if you turn am. Di direction wey dem put am no get anything to do with di name of di shape.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.o.c: Measure whether all di straight lines get same length
y-m-02-01.s.s2.r.c: You use one feature wey you only see for card 가 as di standard. Check whether e work as standard wey leave out di long, thin card 나.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.o.d: Count how many straight lines and pointed corners dey
y-m-02-01.s.s2.r.d: You count something wey fit help decide di name of shape. Na clue wey no dey change even if di shape long and thin or slant.
y-m-02-01.s.s2.explain: How many straight lines and pointed corners dey na clues wey no dey change even if you make di shape bigger or turn am. Size, di direction dem put am, and whether di lengths equal no fit be standard to decide di shape name.
y-m-02-01.s.s3.prompt: Write wetin you go tell Harin. Describe with words one card wey look different from 가 but still na quadrilateral (for example, how long e be or how dem put am), and write reason why dem fit call am quadrilateral.
y-m-02-01.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine stretch card 가 very long or lay am for one side.
y-m-02-01.s.s3.hint.1: Count how many straight lines and pointed corners dat card get too, and put those numbers for your reason.
y-m-02-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: E clear how di card wey you describe with words different from 가?
y-m-02-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You give as reason how many straight lines and pointed corners di card get?
y-m-02-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You think why 'di lengths must be the same' no need?
y-m-02-01.s.s3.model.0: Harin, even very long card na quadrilateral too. E get four straight lines and four pointed corners. Even if e long, dat one no change.
y-m-02-01.s.s3.model.1: Card wey be 가 but lie for one side or slant na quadrilateral too. Even if you turn am, e still get 4 straight lines and 4 pointed corners.
y-m-02-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: Example wey change di direction dem put am without making new shape. Dis one valid too.

y-m-02-02.title: Bigger mean heavier? Lifting am and weighing am
y-m-02-02.goal: See when idea 'bigger is heavier' correct and when e no correct; keep adjusting your judgment each time new information come up, and make pair wey similar in size but seem different for weight.
y-m-02-02.material: Jiho talk, "Bigger is heavier." Teacher talk make dem test wetin Jiho talk. She show two objects each time, you lift dem with both hands, and for di end you check with balance scale. (For balance scale, di heavier side go down.)
y-m-02-02.thinking.0: Decide whether to change or keep your judgment with new information
y-m-02-02.thinking.1: Separate cases where e correct from cases where e no correct
y-m-02-02.thinking.2: Decide one way to check am by yourself
y-m-02-02.prereq.0: Experience of lifting two objects with both hands and saying heavy/light
y-m-02-02.prereq.1: Knowing say for balance scale (seesaw), di side wey go down na di heavier one.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.prompt: Each time new information come up, think which side go heavy. When new information show, e okay to keep your thought or change am.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.hint.0: Look each information and first talk one thing wey be the same and one thing wey different from di last pair.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.hint.1: Talk which point from dis information your chosen answer depend on.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.info: First pair: two stones of the same kind. One big like fist, and one small like chestnut.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.ask: Which side you think go heavy?
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.after: If na di same kind of stone, e fine to guess say di big one heavier, or talk say you go decide after lifting dem. For dis pair, 'bigger is heavier' fit well.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Dis use di idea say when na di same kind, di bigger one get more material inside.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: No clue dey yet to make you think di small one heavier. Remember which clue make you think so.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.o.c: E hard to decide before lifting dem
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Dis na careful idea wey wan check first. Think too how many clues dey.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.info: When dem lift dem with both hands, di hand wey hold di big stone go down more. Di second pair na different kinds. One na sponge ball wey big like two palms (e sink inside when you press am), and one na steel marble wey small like thumbnail.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.ask: Dis time, which side you think go heavier?
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.after: Just because di first pair correct, you no fit use di same idea for dis pair. Na because di material different. Both di guess say di steel marble seem heavier and di statement say e hard to decide with size alone fit.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You carry over di idea wey correct for first pair as e be. For dis pair, first check whether di material na the same.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You use di material difference (sponge wey you fit press and hard steel) as clue.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Di material different, so e hard to decide with size alone
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You see say clue apart from size dey needed. Think too wetin to do to check am.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.info: When dem put am for balance scale, di side with small steel marble go down. Di side with big sponge ball go up.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.ask: How e good to correct Jiho words "Bigger is heavier"?
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.after: E help for objects of di same kind, but when di kinds different, size alone no fit decide weight. So 'always' too strong; even if you guess by size, e more reliable to check by lifting am or using scale.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.o.a: E no always so. When na di same kind, di bigger one heavier, but when di kinds different, e different.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.r.a: I split am into di two stones and di two pairs of sponge and steel marble, then talk am.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Size no matter at all. Di smaller one heavier.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You stretch di result from one pair to cover every case. Remember again how di stones for di first pair be.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Jiho correct. Di sponge ball bigger, so di scale wrong.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: When expectation and result different, you doubt di result. Look again wetin you check with di scale.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.o.d: No decide with size; you gatz check by lifting am or putting am on scale.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You choose method to check directly instead of following size.
y-m-02-02.s.s1.reflect: For first pair, di idea 'di big stone heavier' na judgment wey you fit keep; for second pair, new information say di material different mean say you no fit use di idea just as e be. Di main point of dis activity na to talk up to which information your idea correct by adding conditions.
y-m-02-02.s.s2.prompt: Write one pair of two objects wey look similar in size but seem quite different in weight. Write how you go check dem too.
y-m-02-02.s.s2.hint.0: Think two objects for your classroom or house, and first compare their sizes.
y-m-02-02.s.s2.hint.1: Think wetin you go feel if you hold each object for one hand, and which side go go down if you put dem on scale.
y-m-02-02.s.s2.placeholder: Example: ... and ... similar in size, but ...
y-m-02-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Di two objects wey you choose really similar in size?
y-m-02-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You decide which one of di two objects you think heavier?
y-m-02-02.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You fit really compare their weight with di method wey you write?
y-m-02-02.s.s2.model.0: Cotton ball and pebble similar in size, but I think pebble heavier. I go check by holding one for each hand or putting dem on balance scale.
y-m-02-02.s.s2.model.1: Empty box and box wey get books inside na di same size, but di one with books heavier. If I put dem on seesaw, I fit tell which side go down.
y-m-02-02.s.s2.modelNote.1: Example wey di things inside one object different dey valid too.

y-m-02-04.title: Tall cup fit hold more water?
y-m-02-04.goal: Choose reliable ways to test idea "tall cup hold more," judge by pouring result, and describe cup shapes where this idea wrong.
y-m-02-04.material: Cup 가 tall and narrow. Cup 나 short and very wide. Both open at top, smooth inside. Ain say, "가 taller, so e hold more water." Junho say, "Make we no trust eyes; test with water."
y-m-02-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose all reliable ways to find which cup hold more water.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.hint.0: Besides looking, think how to compare cups using actual water.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.hint.1: For each method, say what e measure or compare, and check if that same as "amount of water e fit hold."
y-m-02-04.s.s1.o.a: Put two cups side by side and look only at height
y-m-02-04.s.s1.r.a: Height na only one clue. You no know how wide cup be.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.o.b: Pour water from full cup 가 into cup 나 and look
y-m-02-04.s.s1.r.b: This method pour water directly to compare cup sizes. Also think how to read result.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.o.c: Lift am and choose heavier cup
y-m-02-04.s.s1.r.c: You weigh cup itself. Think if na same as amount water e hold.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.o.d: Count how many times each fill with same small container
y-m-02-04.s.s1.r.d: This method use same container as unit and same standard to compare both cups.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.explain: Pouring water directly or counting fills with same container fit compare capacity whatever cup shape. Height only or lifting empty cups no compare water amount directly.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.acc.0: Pouring alone fit give reliable result. Good to know counting with same container too.
y-m-02-04.s.s1.acc.1: Counting fills with same small container reliable too. Good to know pouring method too.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.prompt: Junho fill cup 가 with water and pour all into cup 나 without spill; water for 나 reach only about halfway. Wetin we fit say from this?
y-m-02-04.s.s2.hint.0: Say in words both say cup 가 water was full, and cup 나 no fill from that water.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.hint.1: After pouring all from 가, draw how full 나 become and whether empty space remain.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.r.a: You read poured water no fill cup and compare cup sizes.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.r.b: You put first thought about height before result. Think wetin mean say all water of 가 move and 나 no full.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.o.c: Both cups hold same water amount
y-m-02-04.s.s2.r.c: Check whether water wey fill one cup also fill cup 나.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.o.d: No judge before try one more time
y-m-02-04.s.s2.r.d: Checking once more good habit. But if all water move without spill, think what this result alone let you say.
y-m-02-04.s.s2.explain: Water wey fill cup 가 reach only halfway of cup 나, so 나 fit hold more water. First idea (taller cup hold more) no correct for these cups.
y-m-02-04.s.s3.prompt: Describe two new cups (다 and 라) where Ain claim "taller means more water" may fail. Make dem different from 가 and 나; write height and width with numbers or words (e.g. height 20 cm, width 3 cm), and say which hold more.
y-m-02-04.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine two cups with values different from 가 and 나 (height, width). Think what differ besides height.
y-m-02-04.s.s3.hint.1: Imagine fill both cups to same height and compare which holds more water.
y-m-02-04.s.s3.placeholder: For example, cup 다 na ... and cup 라 na ...
y-m-02-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: For cups 다 and 라 you draw, clear which taller and which wider?
y-m-02-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did short cup, no be tall one, come out holding more water?
y-m-02-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You fit check whether my statement correct by pouring or counting with same container?
y-m-02-04.s.s3.model.0: Cup 다 20 cm tall but thin; cup 라 8 cm tall but very wide. Short wide cup 라 hold more.
y-m-02-04.s.s3.model.1: Cup 다 tall but narrow, width 3 cm; cup 라 10 cm tall and wide, width 12 cm. Cup 라 fit hold more. Pour 다 water into 라 to check.
y-m-02-04.s.s3.modelNote.1: An answer wey also add method to check.

y-m-02-06.title: Decorate poster with 8 pieces: which ways possible?
y-m-02-06.topic: Plane figures: decorate with shape pieces
y-m-02-06.goal: Find several combinations of shape-piece counts meeting conditions, and compare systematic ways to find all without missing.
y-m-02-06.material: Saerom class decorate poster using triangle, quadrilateral, and circle pieces. Need 8 pieces total. Three conditions: ① use at least one of each type. ② quadrilateral count less than triangle count. ③ total 8 pieces. (No picture; think only about counts.)
y-m-02-06.thinking.1: Find different answers under same conditions
y-m-02-06.thinking.2: Evaluating ways to find dem without missing any
y-m-02-06.prereq.0: Knowing triangle, quadrilateral, and circle shapes
y-m-02-06.prereq.1: Counting numbers up to 10 and comparing 'more / fewer'
y-m-02-06.prereq.2: Pairing numbers up to 10 (for example, pairs wey split 8 into two)
y-m-02-06.s.s1.prompt: Four friends decide di number of pieces. Choose plans wey no keep di conditions. (Two or more fit dey.)
y-m-02-06.s.s1.hint.0: For each plan, check di three conditions one by one. First count all di pieces and see whether dem be 8.
y-m-02-06.s.s1.hint.1: After dat, put number of quadrilateral pieces side by side with number of triangle pieces and compare which one fewer.
y-m-02-06.s.s1.explain: Line 2 (Haeun) and line 4 (Seoa) no keep di conditions. Haeun get 8 pieces, but quadrilateral pieces no fewer than triangle pieces (2 and 2). Seoa get fewer quadrilateral pieces than triangle pieces, but all di pieces together make 9. Lines 1 and 3 keep all three conditions.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different ways to choose number of pieces wey keep all three conditions. Write a as triangles, b as quadrilaterals, and c as circles.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.hint.0: Decide say 1 quadrilateral piece dey and think about number of di other pieces.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.hint.1: First decide how many triangles and circles must dey together, then check whether triangles plenty pass quadrilaterals.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.ok.c1: All di numbers of pieces na natural numbers.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Di numbers of pieces must be numbers wey you fit count and talk, like 0, 1, 2, ....
y-m-02-06.s.s2.ok.c2: You use at least one of all three shapes.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.fail.c2: You must use at least one triangle, one quadrilateral, and one circle.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.ok.c3: Quadrilateral pieces fewer than triangle pieces dey.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.fail.c3: Quadrilateral pieces no fewer than triangle pieces.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.fail.c4: Altogether, e no be 8 pieces. Count all three numbers.
y-m-02-06.s.s2.explain: 9 pairs of numbers of pieces altogether dey wey keep di conditions. E okay to find only one, but e important to check whether several different pairs dey.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.prompt: How you fit find all possible pairs of numbers of pieces without missing any? Choose all di suitable ways.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.hint.0: Arrange di pairs wey you find for table, and separate dem so one row get 1 quadrilateral, di next row 2 quadrilaterals, and so on.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.hint.1: When 1 quadrilateral piece dey, check one by one from how many to how many triangles fit dey.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.o.a: Look for dem as dem come to mind and stop when nothing else come to mind
y-m-02-06.s.s3.r.a: No way dey to check whether you miss anything. Think how you fit know say all di pairs wey you find na all.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.o.b: Fix di number of quadrilateral pieces one by one and separate di rest
y-m-02-06.s.s3.r.b: Dis na method of fixing one thing and changing di rest in order.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.o.c: Find only one way wey use di most triangles
y-m-02-06.s.s3.r.c: You think say you don finish once you find one example. Dis activity dey check whether several ones fit dey.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.o.d: Fix di number of circle pieces one by one and separate di rest
y-m-02-06.s.s3.r.d: Dis na method of fixing another thing and changing di rest in order. Think whether you fit find all without missing any, whichever shape you fix.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.explain: If you fix number of one shape and change di rest one by one, you fit know how far you don search, so you fit find all without missing any. If you look for things as dem come to mind or stop after one, you no fit know whether you miss one pair.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.acc.0: Di method of fixing di number of quadrilateral pieces fit help you find dem all without missing any. Di method of fixing circles na di same way.
y-m-02-06.s.s3.acc.1: Di method of fixing di number of circle pieces too fit help you find dem all without missing any. Di method of fixing quadrilaterals na di same way.
